From: Meredith Allen <meredith.allen@meridiancare.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MeridianCare RFP — legal clarifications needed re IP & liability

Rachel,

Thanks for the RFP submission. Our legal team reviewed the draft annex and has three primary open items we need your position on before our procurement committee meeting on 2025-09-15:

1) IP assignment vs license for custom connectors: does Redwood require assignment of deliverables or will you accept a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license back to MeridianCare?
2) Liability cap: the RFP indicates a cap tied to fees. Please confirm the lookback period (12 months?) and whether security exceptions apply (data breach, gross negligence).
3) Indemnity for third-party claims: our counsel asks whether Redwood will provide IP indemnity for open-source dependencies used in deployed models.

Can you send proposed redline language for the annex and a short risk table for our executive review? Attaching the MeridianCare questionnaire for reference.

Meredith
Meredith Allen
Head of Procurement — MeridianCare
Attachments: Meridian_RFP_Legal_Qs_Sept8.pdf
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Sep 2025 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MeridianCare RFP — legal clarifications needed re IP & liability

Meredith —

Appreciate the clear list. High-level answers below and attached a risk table plus a proposed IP annex for your counsel to review:

1) Custom connectors/deliverables: Redwood's standard position is to grant customers a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use deliverables for internal business purposes. We do not seek assignment of customer's background IP; for Redwood-developed config/connector code specific to your integration, we propose a customer license with a limited source-code escrow option upon request.

2) Liability cap: We propose a cap equal to the greater of (i) fees paid in the prior 12 months and (ii) $250,000, with carve-outs for (a) willful misconduct and (b) data breach and (c) breach of confidentiality. Open to negotiating level; see attached Redwood_Risk_Table.pdf for tradeoffs.

3) IP indemnity: We will indemnify for third-party claims alleging Redwood's deliverables infringe a third party's IP, subject to our standard defenses and limitation to the customer's use as permitted. We cannot assume liability for open-source components' pre-existing licenses beyond warranty of compliance.

I've attached Meridian_RFP_IP_Annex_v1.xlsx with inline suggested language (comments in column D) and Redwood_Risk_Table.pdf. Happy to hop on a 30-min call with your counsel to walk through the redlines. Proposed times: Thu 9/11 10:00 PT or Fri 9/12 14:00 PT — please pick one.

Thanks,

Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Risk_Table.pdf, Meridian_RFP_IP_Annex_v1.xlsx

Subject: RE: MeridianCare RFP — legal clarifications needed re IP & liability

Andrew/Meredith,

Thanks for the feedback and the marked redlines. Redwood's legal position summarized with suggested compromise language below — aim is to close on commercial terms without exposing material IP risk.

1) Background IP / Deliverables: We'll accept a split: background IP remains Redwood's; customer-specific deliverables will be licensed to MeridianCare on a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free basis. For modules where MeridianCare provides unique datasets and we produce custom code that is tightly coupled to that data, we will discuss source-code escrow for an agreed trigger (e.g., insolvency or support termination). Suggested clause: "Redwood retains all rights in Background IP. Customer is granted a perpetual, non-exclusive license to Deliverables, with source-code escrow available upon mutual agreement." (see attached language excerpt).

2) Residuals: Redwood standard residuals clause (allowing general knowledge and skills to be used by engineers) is acceptable. We'll limit it explicitly to exclude use or incorporation of MeridianCare Confidential Information or Protected Data.

3) Open-source: Redwood will provide an OSS notice list on request and will reasonably remediate license conflicts related to our distribution artifacts; we cannot guarantee remediation for third-party modules embedded by customer modifications to the deployed model.

4) Liability cap: We'll agree to the greater of fees paid in prior 12 months or $250,000, with carve-outs for willful misconduct, data breach, and gross negligence. For MeridianCare enterprise terms we can discuss raising the cap subject to volume commitments — please have procurement confirm target band level and we'll run pricing impact.

Next steps:
- Rachel: please share the updated annex with the redlines accepted/modified (I can provide final legal text if counsel prefers).
- Meredith/Andrew: confirm whether you want source-code escrow language included as a firm option.
- I'll prepare a short risk matrix to attach to the SOW/order form and can incorporate the final cap into the order form (we typically place monetary caps in the Master Agreement and order-specific SLAs in the order form).

Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal — Redwood Inference
